cards.title: Frogs swallow food by pulling their eyeballs down into their mouths
cards.body: Frogs don't just use their tongues and throat muscles to eat—they use their eyes. Because a frog has a thin, flexible palate and weak swallowing muscles, it retracts its eyeballs deep into its skull sockets when eating. The back of the eye bulges directly into the roof of the mouth, acting like mechanical pistons that physically shove food down into the stomach. Without blinking, a frog struggles to swallow large prey.

sources.title: Do frogs use their eyes to swallow?

cards.title: Naked mole-rats are completely immune to the burning pain of acid
cards.body: Pouring concentrated acid or chili pepper juice on most mammals triggers agonizing burning. Naked mole-rats, however, feel absolutely nothing. Living in subterranean, poorly ventilated tunnels, carbon dioxide builds up to levels that would convert moisture in typical mammalian skin into painful carbonic acid. Mole-rats evolved an altered nerve receptor that completely shuts down in acidic environments, allowing them to sleep peacefully in air that would leave other animals in excruciating pain.

sources.title: Selective inflammatory pain insensitivity in the African naked mole-rat

cards.title: Hens can spontaneously transform into roosters
cards.body: Under rare conditions, an egg-laying hen can physically transform into a rooster. Female birds develop only their left ovary; their right gonad remains dormant and undeveloped. If disease, an infection, or a tumor damages the left ovary, that dormant right gonad can awaken and develop into an 'ovotestis' that pumps out testosterone. The hen then stops laying eggs, sprouts male plumage and spurs, grows an enlarged comb, and begins crowing at dawn.

sources.title: Can a Chicken Really Change Its Sex?

cards.title: An octopus has three hearts, and swimming stops the biggest one
cards.body: An octopus powers its circulation with three separate hearts. Two branchial hearts pump blue, copper-rich blood through the gills to collect oxygen, while a central systemic heart circulates oxygenated blood through the rest of the body. Curiously, the systemic heart stops beating whenever an octopus swims, quickly exhausting the animal. Because swimming literally cuts off its own main circulation, an octopus prefers slowly crawling along the seafloor rather than swimming.

sources.title: Octopuses have three hearts: here's why

cards.title: Cashews grow outside of fruit and have poison-ivy shells
cards.body: Cashews do not grow inside normal pods or nuts. Each cashew grows dangling beneath a plump, pear-shaped false fruit known as a cashew apple. Stranger still, the cashew's shell contains an oily resin packed with anacardic acid and urushiol—the exact same toxic compound found in poison ivy. Shelling a raw cashew causes severe skin blistering, which is why commercial cashews are always roasted or steamed to destroy the toxins before being sold.

quizzes.question: Why do frogs pull their eyeballs down into their heads while eating?
options: To mechanically shove swallowed prey down into their throats
To shield their corneas from struggling insect legs
To equalize internal fluid pressure inside their skull
To trigger saliva production through muscle compression
quizzes.explanation: Because frogs lack strong swallowing muscles and hard palates, retracting their eyes pushes food down the esophagus.

quizzes.question: Why are naked mole-rats completely immune to acid pain?
options: A genetic mutation in their nerve receptors blocks acid signaling
Their skin is coated in an alkaline mucus that neutralizes acid
They completely lack sensory pain fibers throughout their body
Subterranean sulfur deposits desensitized their nervous system
quizzes.explanation: To survive high carbon dioxide levels in crowded burrows, mole-rats evolved altered nerve receptors that shut down in acidic conditions.

quizzes.question: How can an adult female chicken spontaneously transform into a rooster?
options: Damage to the left ovary allows a dormant right gonad to become an ovotestis
A severe drop in coop temperature activates hidden male genes
Excess dietary calcium permanently reverses estrogen production
Mating season stress causes the pituitary gland to produce testosterone
quizzes.explanation: Female birds typically rely on a single left ovary. If it fails, the dormant right gonad can awaken and produce testosterone.

quizzes.question: What happens to an octopus's central systemic heart while it swims?
options: It temporarily stops beating
It beats twice as fast as the other two hearts
It reverses the flow of oxygenated blood
It switches from pumping blue blood to red blood
quizzes.explanation: Swimming stops the main systemic heart, rapidly tiring the octopus and making it prefer crawling along the seabed.

quizzes.question: Why are cashews never sold in grocery stores inside their natural shells?
options: The shells contain urushiol, the blistering chemical found in poison ivy
The shells are completely impervious to standard commercial nutcrackers
The shells release toxic cyanide gas when exposed to air
The shells absorb moisture and rot within hours of being picked
quizzes.explanation: Cashew shells contain toxic anacardic acid and urushiol, which cause severe chemical burns unless removed by roasting or steaming.

guesses.prompt: How many hearts does an octopus have pumping blood through its body?
guesses.explanation: An octopus has two branchial hearts pumping blood through the gills and one central systemic heart for the rest of its body.

misconceptions.claim: Frogs blink while swallowing simply to protect their eyes from struggling prey
misconceptions.explanation: Frogs pull their eyeballs deep into their skulls to physically force food down their throat.

misconceptions.claim: Concentrated acid and capsaicin trigger burning pain in all mammals
misconceptions.explanation: Naked mole-rats possess an altered nerve channel that prevents them from feeling acid and capsaicin pain.

misconceptions.claim: An egg-laying hen can naturally transform into a crowing rooster
misconceptions.explanation: If a hen's functioning left ovary is damaged, her dormant right gonad can develop into an ovotestis, turning her into a rooster.

misconceptions.claim: Raw cashews sold in grocery stores are completely unprocessed and unheated
misconceptions.explanation: Cashews must be thoroughly roasted or steamed to remove urushiol, the blistering toxin found in poison ivy.
